metadata.name: Sample L1/L2 Troubleshooting Knowledge Base
metadata.disclaimer: Simulated sample data created for an internship assessment. These are NOT real production incidents or official runbooks of any company. Thresholds, team names, and procedures are illustrative assumptions.

entries.title: Payment API returning HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
symptoms: Payment API (for example POST /v1/payments) returns HTTP 500
Spike in 5xx error rate on the API monitoring dashboard
Merchants report 'payment failed' or 'something went wrong' at checkout
Application logs show unhandled exceptions or stack traces
diagnostic_checks: Confirm scope on the monitoring dashboard: are all requests failing, or only one merchant, endpoint, or payment method?
Search application logs around the first error timestamp for exceptions and stack traces; note the request or correlation IDs.
Check for recent changes in the last 24 hours: deployments, configuration changes, or feature-flag updates.
Check the health of downstream dependencies on dashboards: database, cache, authentication service, and card network or acquirer gateway.
Check application host or pod resources: CPU, memory, thread pools, and recent restarts or OOMKilled events.
resolution_steps: If errors began right after a deployment, share the evidence (timestamps, error rate, sample request IDs) with the release owner for a rollback decision.
If a downstream dependency is failing, follow that dependency's knowledge-base entry (for example KB-003 for database connection failures).
If the failure is limited to one merchant or payload pattern, capture masked sample requests and request IDs for L2 analysis.
Never copy full card numbers (PAN) or other sensitive cardholder data into tickets or chat.
requires_approval: Rolling back a production deployment
Restarting application services or pods
Changing production configuration or feature flags

escalation.when: 5xx error rate stays above 2% for more than 5 minutes, or multiple merchants report payment failures.
Payments are failing platform-wide: declare a major incident and open an incident bridge.

prerequisites: Read access to the log platform and APM dashboards
Access to deployment and change history

entries.title: API requests timing out (HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout)
symptoms: Clients receive HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout or 'request timed out' errors
Requests hang and then fail after a fixed time such as 30 or 60 seconds
Load balancer or API gateway logs show upstream timeout errors
Payment status is unknown to the merchant because the response never arrived
diagnostic_checks: Check API gateway or load balancer logs to see which upstream service is timing out.
Compare the configured timeout values of the client, gateway, and backend service.
Check backend response-time percentiles (p95/p99) on the APM dashboard for the affected endpoint.
Check whether a slow downstream call (database query, third-party gateway, or card network) is causing the delay.
For payment requests, verify the final transaction status using the request ID before advising any retry, to avoid duplicate charges.
resolution_steps: If one downstream dependency is slow, follow its knowledge-base entry (KB-003 for database, KB-007 for network).
Advise merchants to use the transaction status-check API before retrying a timed-out payment.
Share APM traces of the slow requests with L2 Application Support for code- or query-level analysis.
requires_approval: Changing timeout values on the gateway or service
Scaling services up or down in production

escalation.when: Timeouts affect more than 1% of requests for over 5 minutes or a critical payment endpoint.
Timeouts originate at the load balancer or gateway layer, or affect multiple unrelated services.

prerequisites: Access to API gateway logs and APM traces

entries.title: Database connection failures or connection pool exhausted
symptoms: Application logs show 'could not connect to database', 'connection refused', or 'connection timed out'
Errors such as 'connection pool exhausted', 'too many connections', or 'unable to acquire JDBC connection'
APIs that read or write data fail while static or health endpoints still work
Sudden increase in HTTP 500 errors linked to database calls
diagnostic_checks: Check the database monitoring dashboard: is the database up, and what are its CPU, memory, and active connection counts?
Compare active connections with the configured maximum connections and the application pool size.
Look for long-running queries or locks reported by the database monitoring tool (read-only views).
Check whether the failures started with a deployment, a traffic spike, or a scheduled batch job.
Verify network reachability from the application host to the database host and port (see KB-007).
resolution_steps: If the database is unreachable or down, escalate immediately to the Database Team with timestamps and error messages.
If the pool is exhausted because of a traffic spike, share connection metrics with L2 Application Support and the Database Team.
If a specific long-running query or lock is identified, provide its details to the Database Team for a decision.
requires_approval: Terminating database sessions or killing queries
Restarting the database or application services
Changing connection pool or database configuration

escalation.when: Database is unreachable, connections are at the maximum limit, or blocking locks or long-running queries are found.
The database is healthy but the application pool is exhausted or leaking connections.

prerequisites: Read-only access to database monitoring dashboards

entries.title: Authentication failures (HTTP 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden)
symptoms: API returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden
Errors such as 'invalid API key', 'token expired', or 'invalid signature'
A merchant or partner suddenly cannot call the API after working earlier
Users cannot log in to the merchant dashboard
diagnostic_checks: Check whether failures affect one merchant or client, or all clients (scope).
Check authentication service logs for the specific reason: expired token, invalid key, wrong environment, or IP not allowlisted.
Confirm the client is using the correct environment's credentials (for example UAT keys against production).
Check whether API keys, certificates, or secrets were recently rotated.
Check the health of the authentication or identity service on the monitoring dashboard.
resolution_steps: If only one merchant is affected and the cause is expired or wrong credentials, guide them through the standard credential-renewal process.
If all clients are failing, treat it as an authentication service issue and escalate.
If the logs suggest brute-force attempts or credential misuse, report it to the Security / IAM Team; do not share key details in open channels.
requires_approval: Regenerating or revoking API keys
Changing IP allowlists or access policies

escalation.when: Suspected credential compromise, brute-force attempts, or a platform-wide authentication service failure.
A single merchant's integration has a signature or token generation problem.

entries.title: High API latency (slow responses but requests succeed)
symptoms: API responses are slow but eventually succeed
p95 or p99 latency alert triggered on the APM dashboard
Merchants report slow checkout or long payment processing time
Latency rises during peak traffic hours
diagnostic_checks: Identify which endpoints are slow and since when using APM latency graphs (p50, p95, p99).
Compare current traffic volume with normal levels to check for a traffic spike.
Use distributed traces to find the slowest span: database, external gateway, cache, or application code.
Check host or container resources: CPU, memory, garbage-collection pauses, and thread-pool saturation.
Check whether latency began after a deployment or configuration change.
resolution_steps: Share the slowest traces and the time window with L2 Application Support.
If resource saturation is confirmed, raise a capacity or scaling request with DevOps / Infrastructure.
If a slow database query is identified, follow KB-003 and involve the Database Team.
requires_approval: Scaling infrastructure in production
Rolling back a deployment

escalation.when: p99 latency stays above the agreed SLO (for example 2 seconds) for more than 10 minutes.
CPU, memory, or node capacity is saturated.

prerequisites: Access to APM dashboards and distributed tracing

entries.title: Service unavailable (HTTP 503) or service down
symptoms: Clients receive HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
Health checks failing; load balancer shows no healthy targets
Pods in CrashLoopBackOff or instances repeatedly restarting
Uptime monitor reports the service as down
diagnostic_checks: Check the load balancer target health and the number of healthy instances or pods.
Check orchestration events (for example Kubernetes pod events) for crashes, OOMKilled, or failed readiness probes.
Read the startup logs of failing instances for configuration or dependency errors.
Check for recent deployments, infrastructure changes, or certificate expiry (see KB-008).
Check whether planned maintenance is scheduled for this service.
resolution_steps: If caused by a recent deployment, provide evidence to the release owner for a rollback decision.
If instances crash because a dependency is unavailable, follow the dependency's entry (KB-003, KB-007).
Open or join the incident bridge and post regular status updates when customer impact is confirmed.
requires_approval: Restarting services or pods
Rolling back deployments
Scaling or replacing infrastructure

escalation.when: No healthy instances, pods crash-looping, or infrastructure-level failure.
A customer-facing payment service is down: raise a major incident.

prerequisites: Read access to load balancer and orchestration dashboards

entries.title: Network connectivity or DNS resolution failure
symptoms: Errors such as 'connection refused', 'no route to host', or 'host unreachable'
DNS errors such as 'unknown host', 'name or service not known', or NXDOMAIN
Service cannot reach a third-party gateway, bank, or internal dependency
Intermittent packet loss or connection resets between services
diagnostic_checks: Identify the source and destination host, port, and protocol that are failing.
Check DNS resolution of the destination hostname from an affected host (for example nslookup) and compare with an unaffected host.
Test basic reachability of the destination port (for example Test-NetConnection on Windows, or curl/telnet on Linux), if permitted by policy.
Check whether firewall rules, security groups, or IP allowlists changed recently.
Check the third party's status page or notifications if the destination is external.
resolution_steps: Share the test results (source, destination, port, DNS output, timestamps) with the Network Team.
If an external partner is unreachable, inform the partner contact through the agreed channel and track their response.
Do not change firewall or DNS records yourself; raise a change request.
requires_approval: Changing firewall rules, security groups, or routing
Changing DNS records

escalation.when: DNS resolution fails, ports are blocked, or packet loss or connection resets are confirmed.

prerequisites: Shell access to an affected host for read-only network tests

entries.title: SSL/TLS certificate expired or TLS handshake failure
symptoms: Errors such as 'certificate has expired', 'SSL handshake failed', or 'PKIX path building failed'
Clients or partners suddenly cannot connect over HTTPS
Browser shows 'Your connection is not private'
Certificate-expiry monitoring alert triggered
diagnostic_checks: Check the certificate's expiry date and issuer for the affected endpoint (for example in the browser or with openssl s_client).
Confirm whether the failure is for inbound traffic (our certificate) or outbound calls (a partner's certificate).
Check whether the full certificate chain (intermediate certificates) is served correctly.
Check whether a certificate was recently renewed or replaced.
resolution_steps: If our certificate has expired or is about to expire, escalate to the team that owns certificate management with the endpoint name and expiry date.
If a partner's certificate is the problem, notify the partner and track resolution.
Record the incident so expiry monitoring can be improved.
requires_approval: Installing or replacing production certificates
Disabling certificate validation (should never be done as a workaround in production)

escalation.when: Our certificate is expired, missing intermediates, or needs urgent renewal.
Certificate trust or key compromise concerns.

prerequisites: Ability to inspect certificates of public endpoints

entries.title: Sudden spike in card transaction declines
symptoms: Decline rate is much higher than normal for card transactions
Many transactions fail with issuer response codes such as 91 (issuer unavailable) or 96 (system malfunction)
Declines concentrated on one bank, card network, BIN range, or merchant
Merchants report 'card declined' for cards that normally work
diagnostic_checks: Compare the current approval or decline rate with the normal baseline for the same time window.
Break down declines by response code, issuer bank, card network, BIN range, and merchant to find concentration.
Check whether declines are genuine customer declines (for example insufficient funds) or technical declines (issuer unavailable, timeout, system malfunction).
Check connectivity and latency to the affected card network or acquirer (see KB-007 and KB-002).
Check for any notifications of maintenance or outage from the issuer or card network.
resolution_steps: If declines are technical and concentrated on one issuer or network, escalate to Payments Operations with the breakdown data.
If declines are genuine customer declines (for example insufficient funds), no platform action is needed; inform the merchant.
Do not reprocess or force-approve transactions.
requires_approval: Rerouting transactions to an alternate acquirer or network
Reprocessing or reversing transactions

escalation.when: Technical decline rate exceeds the baseline significantly (for example double) for more than 10 minutes.
Connectivity to the card network or acquirer is failing.

prerequisites: Access to transaction analytics with masked card data

entries.title: Settlement or end-of-day batch job failed or delayed
symptoms: Scheduled settlement or end-of-day batch job shows status FAILED or is still running past its expected window
Settlement or reconciliation files are not generated or not sent to banks or merchants
Merchants report missing or delayed settlement
Job scheduler alert for a missed or failed run
diagnostic_checks: Check the job scheduler for the job status, start time, and exit code of the latest run.
Read the job logs for the step where it failed and the error message.
Check whether input files or upstream data were available on time.
Check dependencies used by the job: database (KB-003), file storage or disk space (KB-012), and SFTP or network connectivity (KB-007).
Confirm whether a partial output was produced, to avoid duplicate processing.
resolution_steps: Capture the failure details (job name, run ID, failed step, error) and inform L2 Application Support.
Notify Payments Operations about potential settlement delays so merchants can be informed.
Do not re-run the job manually unless L2 confirms it is safe (risk of duplicate settlement).
requires_approval: Re-running or manually triggering a settlement job
Editing settlement files or data

escalation.when: Any failed settlement or end-of-day job run.
Settlement will miss the agreed deadline or merchants are affected.

prerequisites: Read access to the job scheduler and job logs

entries.title: Payment stuck in pending status or webhook not received
symptoms: Payment status remains PENDING or PROCESSING for longer than expected
Merchant did not receive the payment success or failure webhook or callback
Customer was charged but the merchant order shows unpaid
Mismatch between the transaction status in our system and the merchant system
diagnostic_checks: Look up the transaction by ID and check its current status and status history.
Check webhook delivery logs: delivery attempts, merchant response codes, and retry schedule.
Check whether the merchant's webhook endpoint is reachable and returning success (2xx).
Check whether the final status from the bank or acquirer has been received.
Check the message queue or event backlog for delays in status-update processing.
resolution_steps: If the webhook failed because the merchant endpoint returned errors, share the delivery logs with the merchant.
Advise the merchant to use the status-check API to confirm the final transaction status.
If many transactions are stuck, escalate to L2 Application Support with transaction IDs and timestamps.
requires_approval: Manually changing a transaction status
Initiating refunds or reversals
Replaying events or webhooks in bulk

escalation.when: Multiple transactions are stuck, or the event or queue backlog keeps growing.
Customers were charged but transactions remain unconfirmed beyond the agreed time.

prerequisites: Access to the transaction lookup tool and webhook delivery logs

entries.title: Server disk space full or low disk space
symptoms: Disk usage alert (for example above 90%) on a server or volume
Errors such as 'No space left on device' or 'disk full'
Application fails to write logs or files; batch jobs fail
Database or service stops accepting writes
diagnostic_checks: Check disk usage per mount or volume on the monitoring dashboard (or with df -h / Get-PSDrive if access is permitted).
Identify which directories are growing fastest (for example application logs, temp files, or backups).
Check whether log rotation or cleanup jobs have been running.
Check whether a recent change increased log verbosity (for example DEBUG logging enabled).
resolution_steps: Share disk usage details and the fastest-growing directories with DevOps / Infrastructure.
Request a review of log rotation and retention settings.
Do not delete files manually on production servers unless an approved cleanup procedure exists.
requires_approval: Deleting or archiving files on production servers
Expanding volumes or changing storage configuration

escalation.when: Disk usage is above 90% or writes are failing.
The affected disk hosts a database.
